newsitem.title: UK: General Accident posts lower nine month profits.
newsitem.headline: General Accident posts lower nine month profits.

text.p: British insurer General Accident reported a 40 million pound drop in its nine month operating pretax profit on Tuesday to 311 million pounds ($512 million), hurt by severe weather losses in the United States.

General Accident posted a worldwide underwriting deficit of 166 million in the nine months ended September 30 which included increased severe weather losses of 58 million. But the company recorded a 23 percent improvement in its third quarter pretax profits at the operating level of 117 million pounds. ($1=.6069 Pound)

"A feature of the results is our performance in the UK where we continue to achieve underwriting profits in a trading environment that has become increasingly competitive," said Bob Scott, GA chief executive in the results statement.

Britain recorded an underwriting profit of 22 million pounds in the nine month period, down from 110 million in the same nine months of 1995, while in the United States GA's underwriting losses widened 25 million to 95 million pounds over the same period.

GA reported total premium income of 4.787 billion pounds in the nine month period, up from 4.433 billion. Long term life insurance business premium income, which included 275 million pounds from the acquisition of Provident Mututal on January 1, rose to 1.34 billion from 1.131 billion.

"The positive underlying performance in all our major business units worldwide which we reported at the half year has continued during the third quarter and we would expect this trend to be maintained," added Scott.
